packets.packetTitle: Reusable MCP verification ladder -- initialize alone is not sufficient proof
packets.projectFile: N/A -- operational methodology, not a project deliverable
packets.nextAction: Adopt this ladder as the default MCP health-check standard for future estate work
packets.advancementGate: none -- already proven across 5 servers in this mission
doNotAdvance: Declare an MCP 'operational' based on Level 1 (process starts) or Level 2 (initialize succeeds) alone

ladder.name: CONFIGURATION_PRESENT
ladder.description: Entry exists in the MCP client config (e.g. ~/.claude.json)

ladder.name: PROCESS_STARTS
ladder.description: The spawned command/process starts without immediately exiting

ladder.name: INITIALIZE_SUCCEEDS
ladder.description: A valid jsonrpc initialize response is returned

ladder.name: TOOLS_CAPABILITY_DECLARED
ladder.description: initialize's capabilities.tools is present (even if empty object)

ladder.name: TOOLS_LIST_SUCCEEDS
ladder.description: A tools/list request (after the initialized notification) returns a result, not an error or timeout

ladder.name: EXPECTED_TOOL_CATALOG_APPEARS
ladder.description: The returned tool list matches what the server's own source declares

ladder.name: REAL_READ_ONLY_TOOL_CALL_SUCCEEDS
ladder.description: A real tools/call against a safe, read-only tool returns a coherent application-level result (success or a clean structured error -- not a crash)

ladder.name: CLIENT_EXPOSES_AND_CAN_INVOKE
ladder.description: The actual MCP client (e.g. Claude Code) indexes and can call the tool -- this is the level that actually matters to an agent

content.keyFinding: Levels 1-2 passing does not imply levels 4-7 will pass. In this mission, four servers passed levels 1-3 for weeks but silently failed at level 7 (Claude Code showed zero tools) due to a client-side config defect (unsupported cwd), not a server defect -- proven by reaching level 6 via raw protocol probing outside the client entirely.
content.reusablePattern: When an MCP shows as connected/zero-tools or fails ingestion in a specific client, test levels 0-6 with a raw stdio JSON-RPC probe independent of that client BEFORE assuming the server itself is broken. If levels 0-6 all pass cleanly, the defect is in that specific client's ingestion/configuration layer, not the server.

evidenceRefs: custom raw-protocol probe script sending initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/list -> tools/call sequentially over stdio, run against bid-composer-app-mcp (control) and all four flagged servers

packets.packetTitle: Claude Code stdio MCP registration has no supported cwd field (this version: 2.1.235)
packets.projectFile: N/A -- Claude Code client behavior, not a Capital Glass repo
packets.nextAction: Any future stdio MCP launcher that needs a specific working directory must establish it itself (a shell wrapper, or internal process.chdir before any cwd-sensitive resolution happens) -- never rely on a cwd config field
packets.advancementGate: none -- directly reproduced and fixed twice in this mission
doNotAdvance: Assume a 'cwd' key in an MCP server's ~/.claude.json entry has any effect

evidence: `claude mcp add --help` exposes no --cwd flag or equivalent (checked full help output)
`claude mcp get <name>` never displays a cwd field even when one is present in the raw JSON config

Direct reproduction: running the exact same command with an explicit cd into the target repo first succeeded; running it from an unrelated directory (matching what Claude Code would actually do, since it ignores the cwd field) reproduced the identical crash
content.operationalRule: Repo-dependent stdio MCP launchers must establish their own working directory (shell wrapper: bash -c "cd <repo> && exec node ...", or internal process.chdir at the very top before any cwd-sensitive resolution) rather than relying on a client-provided cwd.

evidenceRefs: claude mcp add --help output showing no --cwd option
claude mcp get human-estimator-mcp / bid-composer-command-mcp output before fix: no cwd field shown

packets.packetTitle: tsx TypeScript path-alias resolution (@/lib/...) depends on process.cwd() -- fails silently from the wrong directory
packets.nextAction: Use the deterministic shell-wrapper launch pattern for any tsx-loaded MCP server with tsconfig path aliases
packets.advancementGate: none -- reproduced and fixed for human-estimator-mcp and bid-composer-command-mcp
doNotAdvance: Assume a tsx --import loader launch will resolve TS path aliases correctly regardless of working directory

content.reproduction: node --import <tsx-loader> <script-importing-@/lib/...> launched from the wrong cwd threw: Error: Cannot find module '@/lib/project-parse/door-schedule-review-repository', code: MODULE_NOT_FOUND, traced through tsx's resolveTsPaths
content.secondaryDefectCaughtDuringFix: The first fix attempt used --import node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs (no leading ./). Node's --import flag resolves a specifier without a leading ./ or / as a BARE MODULE SPECIFIER, not a relative file path -- this produced a different crash: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'node_modules'. The leading ./ is required for --import to treat the argument as a relative file path.
content.classification_note: This is TWO distinct, stacked defects, not one: (1) cwd not respected by the client -> tsx resolves aliases against the wrong directory, (2) a missing ./ prefix on the --import argument, discovered and fixed while correcting (1).

evidenceRefs: Direct reproduction command and full stack trace captured during remediation
Second reproduction after the ./ bug: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'node_modules' imported from <repo>/

Final verification: `bash -c "cd /home/wesley/repos/CapitalGlass-BidComposer && exec node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs ..."` -- claude mcp list showed Connected for both affected servers

packets.packetTitle: SUPERSEDED: 'Claude Code rejects dotted MCP tool names' -- disproven
packets.nextAction: Never propose renaming dotted MCP tool names as a fix for a zero-tools-in-Claude symptom without first running the raw-protocol verification ladder (see mcp-verification-methodology-v1)
doNotAdvance: Rename any dotted MCP tool name based on a Claude-Code-exposure theory alone

content.initialHypothesis: Claude Code cannot ingest/expose MCP tools whose raw protocol names contain a literal '.' character, because four servers using dotted names (estimator.*, bidcomposer.*, ce.*, vae.*) showed zero tools while one server using underscore names (app_*) worked
content.whyItSeemedPlausible: Correlation: exactly the four dotted-name servers failed and exactly the one underscore-name server worked
content.disprovingEvidence: Raw protocol probe of the WORKING baseline (bid-composer-app-mcp) showed its own actual tool names are ALSO dotted (app.get_summary, app.get_manifest, ...) -- Claude Code sanitizes dots to underscores for the exposed tool name (mcp__bid-composer-app-mcp__app_get_summary) but this happens identically for a server that works fine, ruling out dots as the differentiator. The true differentiator (proven separately) was the unsupported cwd field.
content.userCorrectionQuoted: The MCP specification explicitly allows '.' in tool names and even uses admin.tools.list as a valid example.

evidenceRefs: bid-composer-app-mcp raw tools/list: 19 tools, all dotted names, e.g. app.get_summary
all four flagged servers' raw tools/list: also fully valid, dotted names, zero errors
